subcategory: uncertainty quantification for fact-checking RAG outputs, conditioned on faithfulness
task: Claim-level hallucination (factual error) detection in RAG answers
problem: Hallucination detectors for RAG conflate factuality with faithfulness to retrieved evidence, labelling correct but unsupported statements as hallucinations.
architecture: FRANQ: estimates the probability that a claim is faithful to the retrieved context (AlignScore) and mixes two uncertainty estimators - one for faithful claims (Max Claim Probability for long-form, Semantic Entropy for short-form) and one for unfaithful claims (Parametric Knowledge likelihood without retrieval for long-form, Sum of Eigenvalues for short-form); optional isotonic calibration and condition-calibration.
retriever: standard RAG retrieval of the evaluated QA systems
generator: Llama 3B/8B Instruct, Falcon 3B Base, Gemma 4B/12B Instruct
knowledge_source: retrieved Wikipedia/web passages of the QA datasets

datasets.name: long-form QA dataset annotated for factuality and faithfulness
datasets.details: new dataset; automatic labelling with manual validation

key_results: Short-form QA (mean of four datasets): condition-calibrated FRANQ PR-AUC 0.711 with Falcon 3B vs 0.705 for XGBoost over all UQ features; PRR 0.541 with Llama 3B vs 0.525 for Semantic Entropy.
Long-form QA with Gemma 4B: calibrated FRANQ PRR 0.401 vs 0.216 for CCP, the best general baseline.
Condition-calibrated FRANQ needs about 300 labelled instances on long-form and about 120 on short-form QA to saturate.
strengths: Separates factuality from faithfulness, matching the practical goal of catching false statements.
Broad comparison with general, RAG-specific and supervised UQ methods across several LLMs; low overhead.

limitations.text: Does not guarantee correct factuality estimates for ambiguous claims, limited evidence or highly uncertain generations; depends on quality of the underlying signals.
Best variant differs across models and settings; absolute PR-AUC on long-form QA remains low (around 0.1-0.17).

title: Faithfulness-Aware Uncertainty Quantification for Fact-Checking the Output of Retrieval-Augmented Generation
